thread:
Joe (Acme): Hey, our users started getting SSO errors right after we rotated the IdP cert this morning. Login flow fails with 'Invalid ACS URL' in the Redwood SAML logs. Can you help?

Maya (Support): Thanks Joe — can you paste the exact error you see in the SP (Redwood) logs or a screenshot of the IdP response?

Joe (Acme): Here is the message from our IdP: "Response to https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/saml/acs does not match allowed ACS list". On our side the metadata shows the new cert and entityID is unchanged.

Liam (Support): Ok looks like ACS mismatch rather than signature at first glance. Two quick checks: 1) Did you re-upload the IdP metadata to the Redwood Console after rotating the cert? 2) Is the ACS URL in the metadata exactly matching the ACS in the app config (including trailing slash / and scheme)?

Joe (Acme): We uploaded metadata. ACS in our metadata: https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/saml/acs (no trailing slash). In our app settings we have https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/saml/acs.

Maya (Support): Can you fetch the live metadata from your IdP and paste the <AssertionConsumerService> entries? Sometimes IdPs include multiple ACS entries and the one signing the response differs. Also check the Response/Assertion Destination attributes in the SAML XML.

Joe (Acme): Pasted snippet: ```xml
<EntityDescriptor entityID="urn:acme:idp">
  <SPSSODescriptor>
    <AssertionConsumerService Binding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-POST" Location="https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/saml/acs" index="0"/>
  </SPSSODescriptor>
  <KeyDescriptor use="signing">
    <KeyInfo>...new cert here...</KeyInfo>
  </KeyDescriptor>
</EntityDescriptor>```

Priya (eng-auth): Quick thought — if the IdP rotated cert and the signed Response is now using a new KeyInfo but the SP (Redwood) still trusts the prior cert thumbprint, signature validation will fail. But Joe's error says ACS mismatch. Two possibilities: 1) The Response was sent to a different ACS (maybe an index other than 0), or 2) Redwood's stored metadata for the tenant didn't get replaced correctly.

Diego (CS): I can see the tenant in our admin panel (tenant: acme-corp). Metadata upload shows a file uploaded at 2025-06-08T09:12:10Z — user: joe@acme. No validation errors on upload. Will check which ACS we parsed.

Maya (Support): Joe, can you run this curl from your IdP host to fetch the metadata and paste the raw XML? Command: ```bash
curl -sS https://idp.acme.example.com/metadata > idp-metadata.xml
cat idp-metadata.xml | sed -n '1,160p'
``` If you can include the <Signature> wrapping element that would help.

Joe (Acme): Done — full metadata attached. One more note: our IdP's metadata has two AssertionConsumerService entries, index 0 and index 1. The index=1 Location includes a trailing slash: https://app.redwood.example.com/sso/saml/acs/

Liam (Support): Aha — that trailing slash could be the cause. If the IdP is sending the Response to the index=1 ACS (with trailing slash) but Redwood's SP is configured for the non-trailing URL, we will reject. SPs typically compare exact URL strings.

Priya (eng-auth): I'll pull the tenant's parsed metadata from the DB and the current SP config. @deploy-bot any recent changes to SAML URL normalization?

deploy-bot: config-change detected: auth-service normalized ACS URLs on metadata upload (2025-06-08T09:13:02Z) by script metadata-normalizer v1.4 — trailing slashes are stripped for stored ACS fields.

Priya (eng-auth): That explains it. The IdP has an ACS with trailing slash; metadata-normalizer stripped the slash when storing in our DB, but the IdP is still sending Responses to the variant with the slash. The SP rejects because the Response's Destination header doesn't exactly match the stored ACS.

Maya (Support): Ok next steps: 1) Priya can either update the SP to accept normalized variant OR add both ACS variants to the tenant's allowed list. 2) Joe can configure the IdP to use the canonical ACS without a trailing slash if possible.

Priya (eng-auth): I'll push a short-term fix: update tenant's ACS allowed list to include both forms (with and without trailing slash) so responses succeed immediately. Then we'll schedule a small change to accept URLs that differ only by trailing slash. Escalating to eng-auth backlog — ticket RA-412.

Diego (CS): I'll coordinate with Joe for the metadata re-upload verification and confirm when users can log back in. Joe — can you re-send a test SAML Response after we add the extra ACS?

Joe (Acme): Will do. One more Q: do you also need the new cert fingerprint from our metadata? Our IdP rotated cert and we want to be sure signature verification is fine.

Priya (eng-auth): Yes please paste the certificate's SHA256 fingerprint from the KeyInfo. If signature fails after the ACS fix we'll focus on cert trust. Example openssl command to compute fingerprint: ```bash
echo "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----..." > idp.crt
openssl x509 -noout -fingerprint -sha256 -in idp.crt
```

Maya (Support): Action items summary: 
- Priya: add both ACS variants to tenant allowed list (in prod) and open RA-412 for normalized-accept behavior.
- Diego: verify metadata upload timestamp and confirm the change applied.
- Joe: run test SSO after we update and paste cert fingerprint if signature errors persist.

Priya (eng-auth): Done — added ACS variant and pushed config for tenant acme-corp at 2025-06-08T09:28:40Z. Patching prod now; should be live in ~2m.

Maya (Support): Thanks team. Joe — please try logging in now and report back.

Joe (Acme): Login successful for me now. Thanks everyone. I also pasted the cert fingerprint in DM for you, Maya.

Maya (Support): Great — marking this resolved for now. We'll keep RA-412 for the more durable fix and confirm with you once that's in QA. :thumbsup:

Liam (Support): Adding a short blurb to internal KB about "ACS URL exact-match pitfalls (trailing slash)" so other accounts don't hit this.

Maya (Support): Closing thread, will follow up in RA-412.
